history.summary: A 1,033sqft 2BR at $1.35M / $1,307 PSF in D05 (Clementi/West Coast, One-North RCR), trading just above the $1,290 URA median on a healthy 48-txn 5.93% CAGR. Reasonable West-side value, but no MRT proximity is listed and the 2002 leasehold faces decay.
history.rating_rationale: 5.93%/yr over 48 transactions is a credible, well-sampled RCR-grade rate, and the price sits right at district median — fairly valued, not cheap. The big caveat is the blank mrt_info field: West Coast pockets of D05 are poorly served by rail, which dents both rental and resale liquidity, and the 24-year leasehold is decaying. A solid hold, not a standout.

history.summary: 99-yr (from 1996, ~69yrs left) D5 2BR priced slightly ABOVE its own recent transactions. The algo's -11.3% 'cheap' signal rests on a single-comparable cohort and does not survive a web check.
history.rating_rationale: Faber Crest's recent transactions sit at ~$1,230-1,266 psf (avg ~$1,266, high ~$1,289), yet this unit asks $1,307 psf — slightly above, not below, market. The dossier's -11.3% age_adj_premium is built on psf_cohort_txns=1, exactly the thin-cohort data quirk the v3.4 prior warns against, so I discount it. The real issue is the lease: 99 years from 1996 leaves ~69 years, with decay and financing/CPF constraints accelerating over a 5-7yr hold. D5 is a solid OCR forward region and the 1,033sqft 2BR is a usable size, but there is no value cushion and a real lease headwind. The 5.93% trailing CAGR (48 txns) is well-sampled history but not a forward guarantee.

catalysts: D5 OCR (realized fwd region ~+4.0%), near Clementi/Jurong East MRT and Jurong Lake District spillover
